newsitem.title: RUSSIA: LUKoil completes Perm refinery upgrade first stage.
newsitem.headline: LUKoil completes Perm refinery upgrade first stage.

text.p: Russia's biggest oil company, NK LUKoil said on Thursday it had finished the first stage of a project to modernise its refinery in Perm, one of the country's largest plants.

A LUKoil news release said the company had spent around $250 million to install a vacuum distillation unit capable of processing 1.6 million tonnes of heavy fuel oil (mazut) a year at the Permnefteorgsintez refinery.
The company had also completed reconstruction of a coking unit with a capacity of 1.1 million tonnes a year to increase yields and produce high quality coke for the aluminium industry.
Permnefteorgsintez, in the central Urals region, has an annual crude intake capacity of 13 million tonnes. It has been running at 92-95 percent of capacity in recent years.
The improvements are the latest in LUKoil's plan to modernise the plant, which began in 1993 with the installation of catalytic reforming, hydro-cleaning and primary refining units.

The release said that the Perm refinery will eventually boost annual output of high quality gasoline to four million tonnes and low sulphur diesel to 4.8 million tonnes, but it gave no data on current output levels.
When total modernisation is completed, the refinery's yield will rise to 88 percent from 71 percent (excluding fuel oil).

LUKoil said it would attract new foreign and domestic credits to complete modernisation of the Perm refinery and that the project was part of the company's overall strategy to modernise all of its refineries by 1998-1999.
"The company plans to boost significantly its income from refining and to raise sharply its profitability in this sector," LUKoil President Vagit Alekperov said in the release.

LUKoil, seeking to produce more European quality refined oil products, wants to boost output of "greener" diesel with a sulphur content of 0.05 percent and of higher grade gasoline. It is already producing LUKoil brand motor and industrial lubricants.
Swedish-Swiss engineering group Asea Brown Boveri AG, through its subsidiary ABB Lummus Global, guaranteed a $96 million loan for the Perm modernisation.
